# React components

Use when building or fixing React UI (web or React Native).

## State and effects
- Keep state as low as possible and derive the rest during render. Do not mirror props into state.
- `useEffect` is for synchronizing with external systems (subscriptions, network, DOM APIs), not for computing values. Most "effect to update state" code should be a calculation or an event handler.
- Every effect that subscribes or starts work needs cleanup. Include all dependencies; do not silence `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`.
- Server data belongs in a data library (TanStack Query, SWR, framework loaders), not hand-rolled `useEffect` fetches with race conditions.

## Rendering
- Stable, unique `key`s from data ids, never array indexes for lists that change order.
- Memoize (`useMemo`, `useCallback`, `memo`) only when a profiler shows a real cost or a child depends on referential equality.
- Split large components by responsibility; colocate styles and tests.

## Forms and accessibility
- Every input has a label; errors are announced (`aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`).
- Buttons are `<button>` elements, links are `<a>`; never clickable `div`s.
- Disable double submits and show pending state.

## Testing
React Testing Library: query by role and accessible name (`getByRole("button", { name: /save/i })`), drive with `userEvent`, and assert on what the user sees, not on implementation details.

## Verify
Typecheck, lint (including the hooks rules), component tests, then check the browser console for warnings while using the changed screen.
